paragraphs.source_en: Coming out of the school gate, I should have gone back to my hotel, but knowing there was no special attraction there I thought I would take a look at the town and walked on and on along the streets just as chance took me. I saw the building of the prefectural government; it was an old edifice of the last century. I saw the barracks; they were not so nice as those of the Azabu Regiment. I passed the main street, and it was not half so wide as Kagurazaka and with much poorer shops. The castle town of 250,000 koku was only great in name. The people who were proud ly calling it by the high-sounding appellation of "castle town" were rather to be pitied than to be envied. While walking with some such thoughts, I found myself just in front of Yamashiroya, the hotel. I expected the town was much larger, but it was so small that there was nothing more to see.
